The Mirning, also known as the Ngandatha, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the coast of the Great Australian Bight, on the southern edge of the Nullarbor Plain, from Western Australia into South Australia. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their country is a long line of cliffs and dunes with very little surface water. Their neighbours were the Ngalea to the north, the Ngadjumaya to the west and the Wirangu to the east. The southern right whales that come to the Bight each winter hold a central place in Mirning law and story.

In 1841 the explorer Edward John Eyre crossed their coast with his Aboriginal companion Wylie, the first European to travel it by land. The East West telegraph line followed in 1877, with a station at Eucla.
